title: Dedicated capacity SLO sizing & prioritization assistant for enterprise intake
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Background: Enterprise customers increasingly request reserved GPU pools with specific SLA targets (p99 latency, sustained throughput) and non-trivial burst needs. Current intake is manual: SEs pass a questionnaire and Eng + PM perform ad-hoc sizing and SLA negotiation. This causes slow response times, inconsistent offers, and more engineering rework.

Goal: Ship a lightweight prioritization assistant for the Dedicated intake flow that produces a justified recommendation for: reserved throughput (tokens/sec or qps), GPU class (A100/H100/T4-equivalent), SLA banding (latency p50/p95/p99 objectives), and suggested scaling policies (autoscale thresholds, burst credits). The assistant should be usable by Solutions Engineers and PMs during initial customer conversations and produce artifacts for Eng onboarding (sizing summary + risk notes).

Scope: Build PM-facing intake scoring UI + engine (rules + heuristics) for customer-provided signals: QPS, latency targets, model family, token length distribution, retention policy, and security constraints. Provide clear rationale, cost tradeoffs, and required engineering work estimate. Integrate result into onboarding checklist and create a standardized response template.

Out of scope: Automated provisioning, pricing negotiation automation, and full-blown ML-based recommendation engine (phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: Solutions Engineers can run the assistant during intake and receive a recommended GPU class and reserved throughput band
Recommendation includes SLO band suggestion (p50/p95/p99) mapped to existing SLA templates and a rationale paragraph
Assistant emits an estimated monthly cost range and identifies >3 implementation risks (e.g., KV cache sensitivity, model quantization impact)
Output formatted as an onboarding artifact (PDF/Confluence template + JSON summary) that Eng can use to create a Dedicated request
Bench: recommendations for 10 canonical customer archetypes match expert panel judgement >= 80% of the time
notes: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with SE and Solutions on common intake signals; collected 42 anonymized intake forms from last 6 months (internal spreadsheet: drive.redwood.ai/intake-2025-Q4).

2026-02-18: PM design session — agreed on 3 UX flows: quick-score (SE-friendly), deep-score (PM/Eng), and exportable artifact. Design to mockups in Figma: https://figma.com/r/redwood/dedicated-intake-assistant

2026-02-25: Engineering spike (ENG-1842) completed. Findings: latency targets below 100ms p99 force smaller batch sizes and higher GPU class; long tail token distributions require higher memory GPUs or KV cache tuning.
2026-03-01: Security review intake opened; KMS/HSM constraints may bump recommendations to private-only deployment. Security owner: Priya Shenoy.

2026-03-04: First prototype scoring ruleset implemented in a Google Sheet + validation harness. Early feedback from SEs: need clearer language for 'burst credits' and a toggle for customer budget sensitivity.
2026-03-06: Design review — added 'confidence band' and an explanation tooltip for each recommendation. Design PRD linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Intake+Assistant+PRD
2026-03-08: Current status: MVP scoring engine + SE quick-score UI demoable. Next: integrate export to onboarding checklist and run 10 retrospective intakes for calibration.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP) — scoring rules + SE quick-score UI + export template (4 weeks)
Phase 2 — deep-score with historical workload calibration and cost model integration (6 weeks)
Phase 3 — automation hooks for Dedicated provisioning and pricing integration (future)
Rollout: Beta with 3 top enterprise accounts + internal SEs, iterate for 2 sprints, then GA
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overconfident recommendations due to incomplete signals. Mitigation: always show a confidence band and require manual approval for P0 customers.
Risk: Security or compliance requirements require private deployments that change sizing. Mitigation: include a hard 'private-only' flag that changes GPU class recommendations and notes KMS/HSM work.
Risk: Cost estimates may diverge from actual infra invoices. Mitigation: calibrate cost model against last 3 months of Dedicated invoices and publish margin of error.
Risk: Engineering load for custom model kernels. Mitigation: flag models that need special kernel work and estimate eng effort in the output artifact.
